answer: Sequential hardware delay registration: each new identity must solve a unique timed puzzle locked to a physical kernel in a secure chip, taking ~10 minutes of wall-clock time and yielding a signed crystal that expires in 24 hours. Registration is rate-limited per device. An attacker wanting N identities must acquire N devices and spend N×10 minutes sequentially, while legitimate users pay only their own device's idle time. The jade token embedded in each chip prevents cloning and binds identity to hardware.
